subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — token volumes, unit econ, continuous batching
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — quick follow-up on token volumes & batching assumptions

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can put together an accurate pricing example and early capacity recommendation: 

1) Traffic profile / volumes
- Average tokens per request (prompt + completion): you estimated ~120 tokens, correct?
- Expected steady-state qps: you said ~15 reqs/sec during peak (roughly 1.8M requests/day). Please confirm.
- % of traffic that is small interactive chat vs. large batch jobs (docs/summarization): you mentioned ~80% interactive, 20% batch.

2) Concurrency & batching expectations
- Are you expecting continuous real-time traffic that can be continuously batched (i.e., many concurrent short requests that can be aggregated on the server side)?
- Any hard latency SLOs for the interactive path (p50/p95 targets)?

3) Budget & unit economics
- Do you have a target $/1M tokens we should aim for in our model? If you have a monthly budget range for inference (ballpark), that helps us prioritize model/quantization/throughput tradeoffs.

Next steps from our side once we have confirmations:
- Produce a short pricing model showing cost per 1M tokens across three throughput scenarios (continuous batching enabled; limited batching; bursty).
- Recommend Dedicated vs Hosted sizing and expected latency impacts at target concurrency.
- Share an SOW draft and a pilot plan (30-day eval + telemetry).

Attaching a simple pricing worksheet we can iterate on.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: pricing_example_1M_tokens.xlsx (Excel template with token/unit econ rows)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow-up on token volumes & batching assumptions

Thanks, Camila — great conversation. Confirming the numbers below and adding a couple more details: 

- Average tokens/request: 115–130 tokens (we see variance by prompt; use 120 as the safe median).
- Peak qps: closer to 20 reqs/sec during peak spikes (roughly 2.5M requests/day at peak day). We expect weekdays peak 9am–6pm PT.
- Traffic split: 78% interactive chat, 22% async summarization/batch. The batch jobs run nightly but are tolerant to higher latency.
- Latency SLOs: interactive path target p95 <= 350ms, p50 ~120ms. If continuous batching causes p95 to exceed 500ms, we'd need fallbacks.
- Target unit cost: we're looking to be in the $40–$80 per 1M tokens range for early negotiation — lower is obviously better but this is our internal target for a production-grade SLA.
- Pilot: Procurement asked for a 30–45 day pilot with telemetry and a seat for our infra team to run load tests.

Let me know if you want sample traffic logs (can share a sanitized csv).

—Alex
VP Product — FinTechCo
alex.turner@fintechco.com
(212) 555-0199

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow-up on token volumes & batching assumptions

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarity. A few notes and clarifying Qs (cc'ing Aditya + Marissa for the sizing / unit-econ calc):

- We'll model 120 tokens/request and two scenarios (steady-state 15 qps; peak 20 qps).
- Continuous batching: sounds like your interactive traffic is highly batchable (many concurrent short requests). That's good — our continuous batching can reduce per-token cost significantly if p95 stays within your 350ms SLO.
- For the pilot, can you share a small sample (1k rows) of request timestamps + token counts so Aditya can run a quick batching sim? If procurement prefers we can take synthetic traces too.

Marissa — can you draft a 1M token unit-econ example (three model options + expected $/1M tokens with and without continuous batching) and include assumed concurrency/batch sizes? Aditya — can you add expected latency impacts per model/quant profile?

Goal: have a 1-page pricing + latency appendix by EOD Monday (Mar 2) so we can send to procurement.

Thanks —
Camila

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing calc + continuous batching assumptions (draft)

Camila / Aditya — draft numbers below. I put this into the attached pricing_example_1M_tokens.xlsx (tab: FinTechCo-draft). Highlighted assumptions at top.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Avg tokens/request: 120
- Steady qps scenario: 15 reqs/sec (1.55M requests/day) => ~186M tokens/day => ~5.58B tokens/month (30-day)
- Peak qps scenario: 20 reqs/sec => ~248M tokens/day => ~7.44B tokens/month
- Continuous batching efficiency: we expect batching to reduce per-token compute by ~30% in the interactive path (due to kernel fusion and increased GPU utilization) at 200–400 concurrent inflight requests. If concurrency drops below ~80, batching efficiency falls to ~10–12%.

Unit Econ examples (per 1M tokens):
- Model A (open checkpoint, 7B, FP16): baseline compute cost ~$12/1M tokens; with continuous batching ~ $8.5/1M tokens. Latency impact: p95 + ~60–80ms at 200–400 concurrency.
- Model B (7B quantized 4-bit): baseline compute cost ~$8/1M tokens; with continuous batching ~ $5.6/1M tokens. Latency impact: p95 + ~40–60ms.
- Model C (13B, quantized + KV cache): baseline compute cost ~$18/1M tokens; with continuous batching ~ $12.6/1M tokens. Latency impact: p95 + ~80–120ms.

Putting it together against FinTechCo target $40–$80 /1M: all model options are well below your target when we combine compute + infra amortized + platform fees. Your target gives room for additional SLAs and retention.

Notes for the pilot: aim for a concurrency window where continuous batching is effective (200–400 inflight). We can instrument a fallback policy to drop to lower-concurrency routing if p95 approaches the 350ms SLO.

I attached the pricing sheet and a quick sim (tab: batch_sim). Happy to hop on a short call with Alex + engineering team to run through.

Cheers,
Marissa
Pricing & Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:46:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pricing calc + continuous batching assumptions (draft)

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple follow-ups: 

- We can share a sanitized 1k-row sample by EOD tomorrow (timestamp + tokens + request type).
- Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide an SLA-backed pilot pricing (trial credits + capped spend) and a short SOW. Can you include a pricing line for a 30-day pilot with up to 50M tokens and a one-time setup fee?
- Also: do you have an example of how the automatic fallback would be configured (rule-based: p95 > 350ms -> route 10% traffic to lower-latency model)? That would help our infra folks approve the pilot.

If those items look ok we can share the sample and kick off procurement.

—Alex

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Pricing calc + continuous batching assumptions (draft)

Alex — great, thanks. Next steps and owners: 

1) Sample traffic: you send sanitized 1k-row sample (Alex) — Aditya will run the batching sim and confirm concurrency windows (ETA 48hrs after sample).
2) Pilot pricing + SOW: Marissa will add a pilot line (50M tokens, tiered overage) + one-time setup. She'll attach a short SOW draft.
3) Fallback rule example: Stephanie will draft a simple rule (p95 > 350ms -> route 20% traffic to low-latency model; escalate if p95 > 600ms -> failover to Dedicated reserved pool).

We can target a DocuSign-ready SOW + pilot pricing by Fri (Mar 6). I'll schedule a short call with your infra lead to review the fallback rule and load-test plan — proposed times attached in the calendar invite.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Camila
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
